My values are: w = $67, x = $88, y = $44, z = $68.

My priorities are: w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2.

I want to rank my schools in decreasing order of value, *within* my Obtainable Set. This is because I will get my highest-ranked school from that set.

The most important aspect of this problem is understanding what schools are obtainable. Since I can't know for sure without more information, I will make some assumptions and consider different scenarios.

Scenario 1: All schools are obtainable. In this case, I should rank in decreasing order of value: x > z > w > y.

Scenario 2: Only some schools are obtainable. I need to consider my priorities. I have high priority at w and y. The other applicants favor y > x > w > z. This means y is likely to be highly competitive.

Since I have a good priority at w, it is likely to be in my obtainable set. Similarly for y. x and z are less certain.

Given the values, I want x most, then z, then w, then y. I will try to get x, but I should protect myself by ranking z second. w has a good priority, so it may be in my obtainable set. I should rank it above y, because it has a higher value.

Therefore, I will rank x > z > w > y. Even if y is obtainable, I prefer w because its value is higher.
